We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target molecule: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We need leaves commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999.

We have some catalog info: aniline with methoxy? Actually COc1ccc(cc1)N is anisidine (para? Actually COc1ccc(cc1)N). That's available cheap (price 6.6 for 1g). Also N4CC(F)C4 is a fluorinated azetidine? Actually SMILES FC1CNC1 (azetidine with F). Price 172.7 for 250 mg, 1298 for 5g, etc.

We also need the heterocycle c2nnn(... )c2N (a triazine? Actually it's a 1,2,4-triazol-3-amine? Let's parse: c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N is a 1,2,4-triazine? Might be a 1,2,4-triazol-5-yl? Anyway we need a building block.

We could consider disconnection: amide bond between aniline (anisidine) and acyl part: NC(=O)- attached to heterocycle. So retrosynthesis: target -> amide formation between anisidine (COc1cccc(N) c1) and acid (or acid chloride) of heterocycle: c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N-COOH (or acyl chloride). So step 1: amide coupling.

Thus leaves: anisidine (commercial) and heterocycle acid (maybe not commercial). Could we get heterocycle via substitution on a triazine? Another disconnection: the heterocycle attached to benzyl group (Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3). So we could disconnect the C-alkyl bond between triazine N and benzyl group via SNAr? Actually the triazine is attached via carbon (C attached to benzyl). Could be formed via nucleophilic substitution of a halogen on the triazine with benzyl amine? But the benzyl group contains a side chain with N4CC(F)C4 attached to phenyl via CH2 (CN4...). So maybe we can form that via SN2 of benzyl bromide with azetidine? Actually we have phenyl-CH2-N(azetidine). So we could have phenyl-CH2-Br (or Cl) reacting with azetidine (N4CC(F)C4) to give the side chain. That is a simple alkylation.

Thus we could have building block: 4-(fluoro)azetidine (FC1CNC1) (commercial) and benzyl bromide attached to phenyl (bromomethyl phenyl). The phenyl also attached to triazine via CH2 (C attached to triazine). Actually the triazine is attached to the phenyl via CH2 (C attached to triazine). So the phenyl has two substituents: one is CH2-N(azetidine) and the other is CH2 attached to triazine (via C). So the phenyl is 1,4-disubstituted? The SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 is a phenyl with a CH2 attached to N4CC(F)C4 (i.e., benzyl azetidine) and also attached via CH2 to the triazine (the Cc3...). Actually the triazine part: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the triazine has a substituent Cc3... (a benzyl group). So the benzyl group is attached to triazine via CH2 (the same carbon that is attached to phenyl). So the phenyl is attached to triazine via CH2 (i.e., phenyl-CH2- triazine). So the phenyl is a benzylic carbon linking both triazine and azetidine substituents? Wait the phenyl has two substituents: one is CH2 attached to N4CC(F)C4 (i.e., -CH2-N(azetidine)), the other is the same CH2 that attaches to triazine? Actually the SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. The leading C is a methyl attached to phenyl (i.e., toluene). So the phenyl has a methyl (C) and a substituent CN4... (benzyl azetidine). The triazine attaches via Cc3... meaning the triazine attaches to the methyl carbon? Actually "C c3ccc(... )cc3" means a carbon attached to the aromatic ring (the methyl). So the triazine attaches to the methyl carbon (i.e., a benzylic carbon). So the phenyl has a methyl group that is further attached to triazine (i.e., a benzylic carbon bearing triazine). So the phenyl also has a side chain CN4... attached to the aromatic ring (para to methyl maybe). So the phenyl core is 4-(azetidinylmethyl)-toluene.

Thus we could get the phenyl core via two steps: start from p-toluidine? Actually we need the phenyl with methyl and benzylic azetidine. Could be built from p-tolyl bromide and azetidine.

Simplify: maybe we can use commercially available 4-(azetidin-1-ylmethyl)toluene? Not sure.

Alternative: we could treat the whole heterocycle with benzyl azetidine as a building block: maybe we can get the heterocycle with a bromomethyl phenyl (bromomethyl tolyl) and then do SN2 with azetidine.

Search for "c1ccc(CBr)cc1" (bromomethyl toluene). Let's search catalog.
